facts: The Project Gutenberg eBook of "Dracula" was released on October 1, 1995.
The eBook can be accessed online at www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/345.
"Dracula" was originally published in 1897.
The text is credited to Chuck Greif and the Online Distributed Proofreading Team.
Jonathan Harker arrived in Bistritz on May 3rd after a delayed train ride.
Harker stayed at the Hotel Royale in Klausenburgh.
On the eve of St. George's Day, locals warned Harker of potential dangers.
Harker encountered a mysterious blue flame during his night ride through Borgo Pass.
Jonathan Harker arrives at Count Dracula's castle on May 5.
Count Dracula has sharp teeth and a pallid complexion.
Harker discovers a library filled with English books in the castle.
Count Dracula destroys Harker's mirror, leaving him without a means to shave.
Jonathan Harker realizes he is a prisoner in Count Dracula's castle.
Harker finds solace in a crucifix given to him.
Harker witnesses Dracula's ability to crawl down the castle walls.
One of the women opens a bag that emits a child's wail.
Jonathan Harker awakens disoriented in Count Dracula's castle.
Harker discovers his belongings are missing while plotting his escape.
Harker confronts Count Dracula and three vampiric women in the castle.
Harker plans to escape by scaling the castle walls and taking gold with him.
Mina Murray expresses her longing to be with Lucy Westenra in a series of letters.
Lucy Westenra received three marriage proposals in one day.
Dr. John Seward is a doctor at a lunatic asylum.
Quincey P. Morris invites Arthur Holmwood to a gathering to celebrate his engagement to Lucy.
Mina Murray arrives in Whitby in late July.
Lucy is engaged to Arthur Holmwood.
Mina expresses concern for her absent fiancé, Jonathan.
Mr. Swales mentions a strange Russian ship behaving erratically.
The storm struck Whitby on August 8.
The foreign schooner _Demeter_ entered the harbor with its helmsman found dead.
The ship _Demeter_ was identified as Russian and carried silver sand and wooden boxes.
Lucy attended the public funeral of the mate and exhibited distressing behavior.
Mina spends a day with Lucy that includes a walk near the lighthouse and a meal at an inn.
Mina finds Lucy in a churchyard accompanied by a dark figure.
Mina receives news on August 19 that Jonathan is recovering from brain fever in a Buda-Pesth hospital.
Dr. Seward documents a sudden change in Renfield, a patient in the asylum who escapes.
Mina Harker travels to Buda-Pesth to be with her fiancé, Jonathan Harker.
Mina and Jonathan Harker have a wedding ceremony shortly after his awakening.
Lucy Westenra is preparing for her upcoming marriage to Arthur Holmwood.
Dr. Seward consults Professor Van Helsing about Lucy's declining health.
Dr. Seward wrote a letter to Arthur Holmwood on September 6 regarding Lucy's deteriorating condition.
Arthur Holmwood offered his blood for Lucy's urgent transfusion.
Van Helsing brought garlic flowers to Lucy's room, insisting they were medicinal.
The narrator felt a lingering sense of dread about Lucy's mysterious illness after the transfusion.
Lucy Westenra expresses gratitude to Dr. Van Helsing for his care regarding the garlic flowers.
Dr. Seward learns from Mrs. Westenra that Lucy's condition improved after the garlic flowers were removed.
Lucy later feels stronger and credits her recovery to Van Helsing after a blood transfusion.
A telegram from Van Helsing warns Seward to keep a close watch on the flowers due to ongoing peril.
Dr. Seward visited Hillingham on September 18 after receiving a telegram from Van Helsing.
Lucy Westenra exhibited severe distress and signs of blood loss when found by Dr. Seward and Van Helsing.
Renfield attacked two men he accused of robbery, resulting in injuries to an attendant.
Mina Harker wrote a letter to Lucy informing her of Mr. Hawkins's sudden death.
Lucy Westenra and her mother are to be buried together.
Van Helsing intends to perform an operation on Lucy's body after the funeral.
Mr. Marquand informs that Lucy's estate will go to Arthur Holmwood.
A golden crucifix was stolen from Lucy.
Mina Harker prepares for a potential confrontation with Count Dracula.
Dr. Van Helsing reassures Mina about Jonathan's mental state after reading his journal.
Dr. Seward recounts Van Helsing's distress over children in Hampstead with puncture wounds.
Van Helsing concludes that the wounds on the children were inflicted by Lucy Westenra.
Dr. Seward has a tense conversation with Dr. Van Helsing about Lucy's death.
Van Helsing proposes investigating a child in the hospital with similar wounds to Lucy's.
Seward and Van Helsing find Lucy's coffin empty when they visit her tomb.
Arthur initially opposes opening Lucy's coffin but eventually agrees to accompany Van Helsing.
The group, led by Van Helsing, enters a dark churchyard to confront Lucy Westenra's empty coffin.
Van Helsing explains that Lucy's coffin is empty because she has transformed into an Un-Dead creature.
Arthur drives a stake through Lucy's heart, resulting in her transformation back to her true self.
Van Helsing rallies the group to continue their quest to confront the source of their troubles.
Mina Harker arrives at the Berkeley Hotel and sends a telegram about Jonathan Harker.
Professor Van Helsing instructs Dr. Seward to meet Mina Harker.
Dr. Seward and Mina discuss using a phonograph to record their findings.
Lord Godalming expresses gratitude to the narrator for her support regarding Lucy's passing.

Dr. Seward's diary entry is from September 30. Mina expresses a wish to meet Renfield, a patient in Seward's care. Morris shoots at a bat during the meeting. Renfield pleads for his release, claiming he has vital information.
Jonathan Harker documents the group's preparations to confront Count Dracula in Chapter XIX of "Dracula."
The group finds many of Count Dracula's earth boxes missing when they enter his house.
Mina experiences a restless night filled with unsettling sounds from Renfield's room.
Mina requests a sleeping draught from Dr. Seward due to her feeling weak and spiritless.
Jonathan Harker investigates boxes linked to Count Dracula on October 1st and 2nd.
Harker speaks with Joseph Smollet and Sam Bloxam about the transport of heavy boxes to a house in Piccadilly.
Dr. Seward observes Renfield's erratic behavior and obsession with souls.
Renfield is found injured, prompting immediate concern from Seward.
Renfield is found gravely injured with a skull fracture.
Dracula is present, holding Mina Harker captive.
Arthur reveals that a brief encounter with Dracula led to the destruction of crucial manuscripts.
Quincey notes seeing a bat leave Renfield's window, suggesting Dracula's escape.
Jonathan Harker's journal entry is dated October 3.
The group plans to search Dracula's house in Piccadilly for clues.
They successfully sterilized the earth at Carfax with sacred wafers.
Lord Godalming and Quincey Morris find eight boxes of earth in the house.
Dr. Seward's diary entry is dated October 3.
Godalming and Quincey Morris report the destruction of Dracula's boxes.
Van Helsing hypnotizes Mina to aid in their efforts.
Mina describes being on a ship during the hypnosis session.
Dr. Seward's phonograph diary is narrated by Van Helsing.
Mina is showing signs of vampirism.
The group discusses Dracula's escape on the ship _Czarina Catherine_.
Harker notes Mina's unease as sunset approaches.
Mina briefly returns to her true self at sunset on October 11.
Mina asks her friends to promise to kill her if she poses a danger.
The ship _Czarina Catherine_ is expected to arrive on October 15.
Mina presents typewritten pages that reveal Dracula's criminal nature.
The group prepares to confront Count Dracula as they travel from Varna to Galatz.
Mrs. Harker undergoes a hypnotic trance to locate Dracula, revealing he is near land but still in his box.
By October 30, they learn that Dracula's box was delivered to Immanuel Hildesheim.
Mina deduces that Dracula is likely traveling by river to return to his castle.
Mina Harker and Dr. Van Helsing journey through the Carpathian mountains towards Bistritz.
Van Helsing discovers the tombs of the vampire women and feels both drawn to and repulsed by them.
Jonathan and Quincey Morris attack a cart believed to contain Dracula, resulting in Dracula's body crumbling to dust.
Quincey Morris succumbs to his injuries after the confrontation with Dracula's body.
